title: Signalpost — Grow as an engineer
intent: Personal skill development: fundamentals, independent delivery and senior responsibilities.

milestones.title: Programming you can explain
milestones.objective: Write, run, test and explain a small program from a blank function.
milestones.lesson: A program transforms inputs into outputs. A variable names a value; a function names a reusable transformation. Parameters receive inputs and return sends a result to the caller. Logging displays a value but does not return it. A condition chooses a path; a loop repeats an action. An array is an ordered collection; an object groups named properties. Trace a concrete example on paper before adding syntax. Files, the terminal working directory and error messages are part of programming. Read FIRST_SESSION.md for a complete first lesson with setup, vocabulary and a 75-minute sequence.
concepts: Values include numbers, strings, booleans and undefined. === compares without coercion.
const prevents rebinding; it does not freeze an array. Avoid changing caller-owned input accidentally.
A test assertion compares actual behavior to a stated expectation; read its first relevant file and line.
Git status lists changes; diff shows edits. Commit only changes you can explain.
milestones.explanation: For 19, count stays 0. For 20 it becomes 1, and 24 makes it 2. The boundary is inclusive because of >=. Empty input never enters the loop, so returns 0. The independent exercise uses a different rule.
guided: Follow FIRST_SESSION.md; confirm node --version in the repository terminal.
Type the temperature example into a scratch file; predict results for [] and [20] before running it.
Change the threshold into a second parameter and explain which lines depend on it.
Run the unfinished U01 checks and read one failure. Seek a concept hint if needed; type the code yourself.
milestones.transfer: Return the first title longer than a supplied length, or null. Define equality behavior and test that boundary.
milestones.drill: Predict what happens when a function logs 7 and its caller adds the return value to 1. Explain undefined from the observation.
milestones.remediation: Trace three values on paper. Write a one-input function before returning to the loop. If the terminal is the obstacle, repeat only FIRST_SESSION setup.

milestones.title: Debugging and problem solving
milestones.objective: Turn an unclear failure into a small reproduction and a verified correction.
milestones.lesson: Start with a precise difference between expected and observed behavior. Reduce the input until the failure is easy to reason about. A hypothesis proposes a cause; an experiment should distinguish it from another cause. Inspect values at a boundary and change one thing at a time. Syntax errors prevent parsing, runtime errors interrupt execution and logic errors can produce plausible wrong answers. Decompose a problem into small operations with explicit contracts. Async work completes later: a Promise represents its eventual outcome, and await can throw when that work rejects.
concepts: A minimal reproduction preserves the failure while removing unrelated code.
Off-by-one errors, accidental mutation and string/number confusion deserve explicit experiments.
Use a breakpoint or targeted log to inspect a hypothesis; remove debug noise afterward.
A regression must fail under the old defect and pass after the correction.
milestones.explanation: Indices 0, 1 and 2 exist; index 3 is undefined. Inspect i and samples[i] to distinguish a boundary error from invalid data. Changing the expected answer would conceal the defect.
guided: Reproduce the example unchanged; predict the first invalid iteration.
Inspect with a log or debugger and correct the boundary.
Write a regression for the original defect.
In a scratch async function, await Promise.resolve and Promise.reject; catch and explain rejection.
milestones.transfer: A search fails only at the last item. Propose two different causes and an experiment separating them before editing.
milestones.drill: A test passes alone but fails after another test. Investigate shared mutable state before adding a timeout.
milestones.remediation: Reduce to two items. Trace indices and values, then reintroduce one condition at a time.

milestones.title: TypeScript and trustworthy tests
milestones.objective: Express valid states in types and verify behavior at runtime boundaries.
milestones.lesson: JavaScript is the runtime; TypeScript checks assumptions before execution. Type annotations do not validate external JSON. Treat external input as unknown, inspect it and narrow to a trusted type. A discriminated union expresses alternatives without contradictory boolean flags. Keep domain decisions in functions with explicit inputs and outputs. Tests should verify caller-visible behavior: ordinary cases, boundaries and failures. Unit tests isolate decisions; integration tests check real components working together. A mock does not prove that its real dependency behaves the same way.
concepts: Learn object types, optional fields, unions and narrowing before advanced generics.
Avoid any and unchecked assertions that hide a missing runtime check.
Make time and randomness explicit inputs when testing decisions.
Coverage alone does not establish that assertions detect meaningful failures.
milestones.explanation: Checking kind narrows the union. value exists only in the found branch. The compiler cannot prove a network response has this shape unless the boundary validates it.
guided: Read Everyday Types and Narrowing in the TypeScript handbook.
Type the example; intentionally read value before narrowing and explain the error.
Run U03 checks and implement one valid-input case with a hint if needed.
Compare a test of output with a test that only asserts an internal call.

milestones.title: HTTP and a small API
milestones.objective: Build and diagnose a small request-response service with explicit error behavior.
milestones.lesson: An HTTP request contains method, URL, headers and sometimes a body. A response contains status, headers and a body. JSON is a representation, not proof of valid input. Trace parsing, validation, domain logic and response separately. A network failure differs from a 400 or 500 response. Start with a single process and an explicitly temporary memory store; persistence comes next. Authentication establishes who is calling; authorization determines allowed actions. This local practice service uses synthetic data and does not claim real user authentication.
concepts: Separate transport, domain rules and storage.
Declare statuses, body limits, missing-object behavior and error shape.
Catch an awaited failure at a boundary that can return useful feedback.
Bind training services to loopback; never put credentials in logs.
milestones.explanation: The server assigns the ID and validates text. Malformed JSON fails parsing; a well-formed invalid object fails field validation. A failed connection has no HTTP response status.

milestones.title: SQL, integrity and transactions
milestones.objective: Persist the API and prove failed changes preserve valid data.
milestones.lesson: A relational schema describes entities and relationships; constraints reject invalid state even when callers make mistakes. Learn SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE and JOIN with tiny datasets before an ORM. A transaction groups changes that commit or roll back together. Parameterize values instead of building SQL with untrusted text. A uniqueness pre-check can race; the database constraint must enforce the rule. Choose indexes from access paths and inspect the plan. Embedded PostgreSQL practice teaches semantics; it does not prove networked concurrency or host-crash durability.
concepts: Keys identify rows; foreign keys enforce relationships.
NULL means missing/unknown; use IS NULL for that predicate.
NOT NULL and CHECK express different promises.
A migration needs populated-data upgrade and recovery evidence.
milestones.explanation: A duplicate id fails. NOT NULL title still permits an empty string. The pages check rejects zero but permits NULL unless a separate NOT NULL constraint forbids it. Test the promise each constraint actually makes.
guided: Run node practice/sql-console.mjs; each statement ends in a semicolon.
Type the books example, then try duplicate ID, zero pages and NULL pages.
Read tutorial joins and transactions; use two or three rows.
Use PROJECTS.md for a file-backed PGlite store in your own API.

milestones.title: Usable interfaces with React
milestones.objective: Build a usable interface with explicit loading, failure and keyboard behavior.
milestones.lesson: Learn semantic HTML and CSS layout before JSX. A button performs an action; a link navigates; a label names a control. React renders from props and state. Keep one owner for a state value and derive what you can calculate instead of duplicating it. Event handlers respond to actions; effects synchronize with external systems. Requests can load, succeed, return empty or fail. Show each state deliberately and preserve user input after failure. Older async responses can arrive after newer ones, so immediate-response tests are insufficient.
concepts: Study HTML forms, box model, flex/grid, responsive widths and visible focus.
Props carry data down; callbacks request change. Use stable IDs as list keys.
A state update requests a render; it does not replace values inside the running handler.
Test keyboard interaction and request ordering as well as the happy path.
milestones.explanation: The button already supports keyboard activation. The updater receives the prior state. A styled div would need additional semantics and interaction behavior.

Make the layout fit 390px with visible focus.

milestones.title: Own a complete feature
milestones.objective: Deliver a bounded feature from a written need through verification and review.
milestones.lesson: Independent delivery connects a user need to dependable behavior through small decisions. Plan a thin end-to-end slice, expose uncertainty and include failures in the estimate. Authorization belongs on the server; a hidden button is not protection. A local server-only test identity seam can test permission rules but does not establish production authentication. Use an established authentication integration before sharing private data with real users. A useful PR explains the final behavior, tradeoff, risk and observed verification.
concepts: Write acceptance examples and non-goals before implementation.
Check membership on every read/mutation, including guessed object IDs.
Keep authentication separate from browser-selected user or project IDs.
Plan verification, failure detection and recovery alongside the feature.

milestones.title: Data structures and measured performance
milestones.objective: Choose suitable data structures and verify performance against a defined workload.
milestones.lesson: Arrays, maps, sets, stacks and queues support different access patterns. Big-O describes growth under an explicit model; it does not predict response time on particular hardware. Recognize repeated scans and unbounded work before optimizing syntax. Define a workload, symptom and correctness oracle; distinguish CPU, I/O and waiting. Compare multiple sizes, warmup and repeated trials. Inspect database plans or browser profiles at the actual bottleneck. Caching adds memory and invalidation obligations.

milestones.title: Reliability and operating a service
milestones.objective: Reason about partial failure and operate a small service using observable evidence.
milestones.lesson: A service can commit while its caller never receives success. Retrying can repeat effects, so define stable request identity and an atomic persistence boundary before claiming idempotency. Bound payloads, queues and retries so overload is visible. Logs should connect symptoms to a user path without exposing secrets. Select a user-outcome SLI and consider needs and data before choosing an SLO. Restore practice matters as much as backup creation. Local drills develop reasoning but do not establish sustained production ownership.
concepts: Distinguish retry attempts from logical application effects.
Use timeouts and a bounded retryable/nonretryable policy.
Readiness, liveness and user success measure different things.
Incident notes connect impact, timeline, evidence and owned follow-up.
milestones.example:

Connection closes before success reaches the client.
Retry R with same payload -> prior result.
Retry R with changed payload -> conflict.
milestones.explanation: If task and receipt commit separately, a crash can leave one without the other. This logical deduplication does not prove an external notification reached a human.
guided: Draw success, pre-commit failure and response-loss paths.
